NSE.name: National Stock Exchange of India Limited
NSE.objects: 100% Offer for Sale (OFS) — proceeds to selling shareholders; no fresh capital to company
NSE.business prose: India's largest stock exchange by turnover, operating a vertically integrated model spanning trading, clearing and settlement (NSE Clearing Ltd), index development (NSE Indices Ltd), data and analytics (NSE Data & Analytics Ltd), and an international exchange for foreign-currency trading. As of March 2026 it held 99.79% of cash-market turnover, 74.71% of equity futures, 99.48% of equity options, and 100% of exchange-traded currency options. FY26 total income ₹18,713 Cr, PAT ₹10,302 Cr.
NSE.sector_outlook: India's equity-derivatives and cash-market volumes continue to lead globally; NSE's monopoly-like cash-market share (99.79%) and diversified non-trading revenue (clearing, data, listings) make exchange earnings structurally resilient to single-trader volatility.
NSE.peer_pe: No pure-play Indian exchange peer is publicly listed for a direct P/E comparison; the closest listed financial-infrastructure proxy is a depositories/trigger platform, so no reliable listed-peer P/E benchmark is available for this sector.
NSE.analyst_why: Monopoly exchange economics with 99.79% cash-market share and 50.98% PAT margin are compelling, but the ₹22,561 Cr issue is 100% OFS (no fresh capital to the business), post-issue P/E of 35.4x is full for an exchange, and subscription at 1.04x day-2 signals tepid retail interest. Anchor books are heavy at ₹6,746 Cr. Listing-day pop likely muted; hold for a post-listing fundamental re-rating, not a quick flip.

Sonaselection India.name: Sonaselection India Limited
Sonaselection India.objects: ₹80 Cr debt repayment + ₹50.61 Cr capex (new plant at Hamirgarh) + general corporate purposes; total ₹130.61 Cr
Sonaselection India.business_prose: Integrated fabric manufacturer and processor based in Bhilwara, Rajasthan, making 100% cotton fabric, cotton-lycra stretch fabric, cotton blends and polyester blends for apparel and textile applications. Installed processing capacity 82.44 million metres per annum across a 49,540 sq.m facility. FY26 revenue ₹517.60 Cr (up 64% YoY), PAT ₹34.02 Cr (up 83% YoY).
Sonaselection India.sector_outlook: Indian textile exports hit a record ~$45 billion in FY25 and the sector benefits from global supply-chain shifts away from China (China+1), plus PLI schemes for man-made fibre and technical textiles. Cotton-fabric processing is more cyclical and price-sensitive than the man-made segment, but the Bhilwara cluster has strong weaving/processing depth.
Sonaselection India.peer_pe: Listed Indian textile-processor peers trade at a wide P/E band; the closest comparable listed fabric/than manufacturers show post-issue P/E in the 12–22x range, making Sonaselection's 16.53x post-issue P/E broadly in line with the cheaper end of the peer set.
Sonaselection India.analyst_why: 64% revenue and 83% PAT growth look strong, but the balance sheet carries D/E of 2.48 with total borrowings of ₹258 Cr, the IPO is barely subscribed at 0.20x day-2 (QIB 0.00x, retail 0.37x), GMP is a thin ₹2 (2%), and the lone lead manager (Choice Capital Advisors) has no 2026 track record. The issue is small (₹141.57 Cr) but the weak subscription and unproven lead-manager bench argue for staying away until the book shows firmer interest.

SS Retail.name: SS Retail Limited
SS Retail.objects: ₹12.45 Cr store fit-out capex + ₹241.35 Cr working capital + general corporate purposes; total ₹253.80 Cr
SS Retail.business_prose: Multi-brand mobile phone, accessories and electronics retail chain operating under 'SS Mobile', 'Mobile Exchange Wala' and 'The Mobile Space' brands through company-owned, franchise-operated and franchisee-only formats. Largest mobile-phone retail chain in western India and Maharashtra; ranked among the top three in India by store count. Acquired 51 franchisee stores in FY26. FY26 revenue ₹2,352.85 Cr (up 47% YoY), PAT ₹59.28 Cr (up 49% YoY).
SS Retail.sector_outlook: India's mobile-phone retail market is large and growing with 5G smartphone adoption, rising disposable incomes and a long tail of Tier II/III cities still under-penetrated. SS Retail's franchise-led model keeps capex light, but thin 2.52% PAT margin leaves little room for error on rent, staff or inventory costs.
SS Retail.peer_pe: Listed Indian retail peers (phone/electronicsSpecialty retailers such as Croma-parent Blume, Reliance Retail unlisted) bracket the space; SS Retail's 53.2x post-issue P/E is richer than most specialty-retail comparables that trade around 25–40x, reflecting the hyper-growth store-count story rather than current profitability.
SS Retail.analyst_why: Subscription at 107.41x (retail 35.81x, QIB 214.22x) and GMP at ₹147 (34.67%) scream listing-day frenzy, and the lead-manager bench (Anand Rathi + Emkay) is strong. But the 53.2x post-issue P/E is expensive versus specialty-retail peers, PAT margin is a thin 2.52%, the issue is working-capital heavy, and the anchor lock-in (30-day cliff on ~146 Cr) creates a near-term supply overhang. Allotted shares may pop on day one, but the exit should be quick rather than a hold.

Jindal Supreme (India).name: Jindal Supreme (India) Limited
Jindal Supreme (India).objects: ₹71 Cr debt repayment/pre-payment + general corporate purposes; total ₹71 Cr
Jindal Supreme (India).sector: Iron & Steel — steel pipes, tubes and structural products
Jindal Supreme (India).business_prose: Manufacturer and supplier of steel pipes, tubes and other steel products for infrastructure and industrial applications, with a Hisar (Haryana) facility housing mills, welding and galvanizing plants. Diversified into W-beam and Thrie-beam metal crash barriers from FY25. FY26 revenue ₹675.94 Cr (up 12% YoY), PAT ₹22.53 Cr (down 7% YoY).
Jindal Supreme (India).sector_outlook: Indian steel demand is supported by infrastructure capex (roads, railways, urban housing) and government push on pipeline networks, but the sector is cyclical and price-sensitive; steel pipes and tubes benefit directly from highway, irrigation and urban-development spending.
Jindal Supreme (India).peer_pe: Listed Indian steel-pipe and TMT peers such as Jindal Steel & Power, SAIL and MP Steels show post-issue P/E broadly in the 8–18x range, placing Jindal Supreme's 14.33x post-issue P/E in the middle of the peer band — neither obviously cheap nor stretched.
Jindal Supreme (India).analyst_why: Subscription at 177.03x (retail 141.75x, NII 326.84x) is exceptional and the post-issue P/E of 14.33x is reasonable versus steel-pipe peers. However, FY26 PAT fell 7% YoY to ₹22.53 Cr despite 12% revenue growth, PAT margin is a thin 3.33%, the issue is mainly debt repayment (₹71 Cr), and the lone lead manager (Sarthi Capital Advisors) has a solid but not stellar track record. Allotted blocks may list with a healthy pop given the GMP at ₹29 (31.18%), but the weak earnings trend argues for a quick listing-day exit rather than a longer hold.

Hero Motors.name: Hero Motors Limited
Hero Motors.objects: ₹190 Cr debt repayment + ₹200 Cr capex (Gautam Buddha Nagar expansion) + ₹nil inorganic/general; total ₹390 Cr
Hero Motors.sector: Auto Components — engineered powertrain solutions (gears, transmissions, e-mobility)
Hero Motors.business_prose: Automotive technology company designing, developing, manufacturing and supplying engineered powertrain solutions to global OEMs. Operations split into Powertrain Solutions (gears & transmissions) and Alloys & Metallics. Customers include BMW, Ducati, enviolo, Formula Motorsport, Hummingbird EV and HWA, plus leading global e-bike manufacturers. FY26 revenue ₹1,216.74 Cr (up 9% YoY), PAT ₹41.17 Cr (up 26% YoY).
Hero Motors.sector_outlook: Global shift to electric two-wheelers and premium ICE/transmission content supports long-term demand for precision gears and e-powertrain components; India's auto-component exports have been growing double-digits, but the segment is capital-intensive and competitive.
Hero Motors.peer_pe: Listed Indian auto-component peers (e.g. modern gear & axle makers, e-mobility-adjacent suppliers) show post-issue P/E in the 25–60x band; Hero Motors' 92.31x post-issue P/E sits well above the peer set, pricing in aggressive e-mobility growth that is not yet visible in current earnings.
Hero Motors.analyst_why: The 92.31x post-issue P/E is extreme versus listed auto-component peers (25–60x), revenue growth is a modest 9%, and subscription at 7.01x is soft (QIB just 1.59x). GMP at ₹-2 (-2.38%) is negative. The lead-manager bench (ICICI Securities, Dam Capital, JM Financial) is strong, which partially offsets execution risk, but the valuation and weak institutional appetite argue for avoiding this issue unless the price band is cut before listing.

Varmora Granito.name: Varmora Granito Limited
Varmora Granito.objects: ₹245 Cr debt repayment/pre-payment (company + subsidiaries Covertek Ceramica and others) + general corporate purposes; total ₹245 Cr
Varmora Granito.sector: Ceramics — vitrified and glazed tiles (Morbi cluster, Gujarat)
Varmora Granito.business_prose: Manufacturer and marketer of ceramic and vitrified tiles (GVT, PVT and ceramic tiles) operating eight manufacturing facilities in the Morbi cluster of Gujarat, with 81.72% of FY26 revenue from in-house manufactured products. Distribution via 305 exclusive brand outlets and 2,758 multi-brand outlets across India and overseas, plus B2B sales to builders and contractors. FY26 revenue ₹1,562.53 Cr (up 5% YoY), PAT ₹55.09 Cr (up 79% YoY).
Varmora Granito.sector_outlook: Indian tile demand is supported by housing growth, infrastructure and commercial real estate; the Morbi cluster dominates national tile production and benefits from scale, export potential and government housing schemes (PMAY). However the sector is cyclical and pricing pressure from China and cheaper imports is a persistent risk.
Varmora Granito.peer_pe: Listed Indian tile/ceramic peers (Vitrifi, Kajaria, Somany) show post-issue P/E in the 25–55x band; Varmora Granito's 60.66x post-issue P/E is at the richer end of the peer set, reflecting the 79% PAT rebound story rather than current earnings power.
Varmora Granito.analyst_why: 5% revenue growth and a 60.66x post-issue P/E make this one of the richer tile-sector IPOs, though PAT rebound of 79% YoY and a clean D/E of 0.45 are positives. GMP at ₹12 (8.11%) is modest and the book has not opened yet. The strong lead-manager bench (JM Financial, Goldman Sachs, SBI Capital) and the Morbi-cluster scale are the main supports; wait for the subscription print before taking a view, and treat any listing-day pop with caution given the premium valuation.
